estimated_study_time.text: Study this chapter in one focused session of about 2 hours, then add extra practice time for timed retell attempts and feedback review.

chapter_summary.text: This chapter practises the PTE Academic Re-tell lecture item type. It focuses on listening for main ideas, supporting points, speaker purpose, vocabulary, explicit and implicit information, sequencing, and variations in tone, speed and accent. It also develops speaking skills for repeating, informing, explaining, organizing an oral presentation, using appropriate language and grammar, speaking fluently at a natural rate, and using correct intonation, pronunciation and stress under timed conditions.

evidence_spans.quote: This lesson provides skills practice for the PTE Academic item type Re-tell lecture.

This lesson focuses on the following skills:  
Listening
• Identifying the topic, theme or main ideas
• Identifying supporting points or examples
• Identifying a speaker’s purpose, style, tone or attitude

• Understanding academic vocabulary
• Inferring the meaning of unfamiliar words
• Comprehending explicit and implicit information
• Comprehending concrete and abstract information
• Classifying and categorizing information

• Following an oral sequencing of information
• Comprehending variations in tone, speed, accent

Speaking
• Speaking for a purpose (to repeat, to inform, to explain)
• Supporting an opinion with details, examples and explanations
• Organizing an oral presentation in a logical way

• Using correct grammar
• Speaking at a natural rate
• Producing fluent speech
• Using correct intonation
• Using correct pronunciation
• Using correct stress
• Speaking under timed conditions

meaning.text: Re-tell lecture is a long-answer speaking item type.

evidence_spans.quote: Re-tell lecture is a long-answer speaking item type.

meaning.text: Content is scored by how accurately and thoroughly the response conveys the situation, characters, aspects, actions and developments in the lecture.

evidence_spans.quote:
Content is scored by determining how accurately and thoroughly you convey the 
situation, characters, aspects, actions and developments presented in the lecture.

meaning.text: Oral Fluency is scored by whether rhythm, phrasing and stress are smooth.

evidence_spans.quote:
Oral Fluency: Oral Fluency is scored by determining if your rhythm, phrasing and stress 
are smooth.

meaning.text: Pronunciation is scored by whether speech is easily understandable to most regular speakers of the language.

evidence_spans.quote:
Pronunciation is scored by determining if your speech is easily understandable 
to most regular speakers of the language.

meaning.text: Note taking acts as a reminder or memory aid, focuses on key ideas or words, and may be brief, abbreviated, or use points, diagrams or mind maps.

evidence_spans.quote:
the purpose and key features of note taking (to act as 
a reminder/memory aid; focus on key ideas/words; brief, abbreviated, may involve points/diagrams/
mind maps, etc)

explanation.text: In Re-tell lecture, instructions are shown at the top of the computer screen. The test taker hears a lecture, then has 10 seconds to prepare and 40 seconds to retell the lecture in their own words.

evidence_spans.quote:
Instructions are presented at the top of the computer screen. The instructions are:
You will hear a lecture.

After listening to the lecture, in 10 seconds, please speak into the microphone 
and retell what you have just heard from the lecture in your own words.

You will have 40 seconds to 
give your response.

core_lessons.title: Expect One Recording And A Short Response Window

explanation.text: The recording plays automatically after three seconds. When it finishes, a 10-second timer counts down before the response. After 10 seconds, the microphone opens and recording starts. The response time is 40 seconds.

evidence_spans.quote:
After three seconds a recording will play automatically. When the recording finishes, a timer will 
count down 10 seconds—the time you have before you respond.

After 10 seconds, the microphone will open and start recording. You have 40 seconds to give 
your response.

core_lessons.title: Use Images Without Letting Them Distract You

explanation.text: Some Re-tell lecture items have an accompanying image. In a test situation, the learner would have 3 seconds to look at the image before the lecture starts. The image can help predict the topic and focus listening, but once the lecture starts the learner should concentrate on listening and taking notes rather than looking at the image.

evidence_spans.quote: Remind test takers that some Re-tell lecture items are accompanied by an image.

Tell test 
takers that in a test situation they would have 3 seconds to look at this image before the lecture starts.

it can help them predict the 
topic/what the lecture will be about and focus their listening

once the lecture 
starts they should concentrate on listening and taking notes, and not look at the image

core_lessons.title: Build The Retell Around Main Ideas

explanation.text: While listening and taking notes, focus on recognizing and noting the topic, the main supporting ideas and their relationship to the main topic, and the conclusion if applicable.

evidence_spans.quote:
their main focus while listening and taking notes during this item type is:
– to recognize and note the topic
– to note the main supporting ideas and their relationship to the main topic
– to note the conclusion (if applicable)

core_lessons.title: Take Notes That You Can Quickly Reconstruct

explanation.text: Effective lecture notes require focused listening, quick recognition of key ideas, supporting points and important relationships, quick distinction between relevant and irrelevant information, fast writing while listening, and a personal abbreviation or shorthand system that can be converted back into meaningful information.

evidence_spans.quote:
to take effective notes from a lecture they must be able to listen in 
a focused manner, quickly recognize key ideas, supporting points and important relationships
quickly distinguish between relevant and irrelevant information.

writing quickly while listening and develop their own system of abbreviations or short hand that they 
can convert easily back into meaningful information.

core_lessons.title: Respond Calmly To Missed Or Unfamiliar Words

explanation.text: If a learner misses or does not clearly hear part of the lecture, they should remain calm and continue listening rather than spend time worrying about the missed part. If they hear words they do not understand, they should remain calm and continue listening because the meaning may not be important or may be explained later.

evidence_spans.quote:
What should you do if you miss or do not clearly hear part of what is said? (Remain calm and 
continue listening.

Do not spend time reflecting or worrying about what was missed as this will 
distract you from the rest of the lecture.)

What should you do if you hear words you do not understand? (Remain calm and continue 
listening.

The meaning of the unfamiliar word may not be important, or it may be explained by 
what follows.)

explanation.text: The speaking part reconstructs the topic, main ideas and possible conclusion of the lecture. The response should start with a topic sentence, present main supporting ideas logically using relevant cohesive devices, and be clear and fluent.

evidence_spans.quote:
the main purpose of the speaking part of this item, type (i.e. to reconstruct the 
topic, main ideas and possible conclusion of the lecture they have just heard).

they 
should remember to start with a topic sentence, present the main supporting ideas in a logical fashion 
using relevant cohesive devices, and speak clearly and fluently.

explanation.text: The Re-tell lecture score is based on Content, Oral Fluency and Pronunciation. The best content responses retell all main points and include possible developments, conclusions or implications. The best fluency responses use a constant and natural rate with appropriate phrasing. The best pronunciation responses contain native-like vowels and consonants and correct word and phrase stress.

evidence_spans.quote:
Your score on 
Re-tell lecture is based on three factors:

The best responses retell all the main points of the lecture and include possible 
developments, conclusions or implications.

The best responses are spoken at a constant and natural rate of speech with 
appropriate phrasing.

The best responses contain vowels and consonants 
pronounced in a native-like way, and stress words and phrases correctly.

example.text: Suppose your notes say: “HDI = ranks nations; not just income; 3 criteria; Norway/Iceland/Australia high.” A concise retell could begin: “The lecture explains the Human Development Index and how it ranks countries. It says the HDI looks beyond income and uses three criteria to compare quality of life. The example image shows Norway, Iceland and Australia among the most livable countries.”

explanation.text: The guided listening sheet asks learners to use questions to guide listening and note taking, and it includes prompts about what HDI is, who publishes it, how it ranks nations, and three criteria for calculating ranking.

evidence_spans.quote: Use the  questions below to guide your listening and note taking.

Who is it published by? 
The HDI ranks nations according to

example.text: Instead of writing “government policies caused an increase in development,” a learner might note “gov’t pol. → ↑ dev.” The note is not a full sentence, but it preserves the relationship and can be expanded while speaking.

explanation.text: The abbreviation list gives examples for government, leads to or causes, and increasing or leading to an increase.

example.text: A useful retell could open with the topic, then connect the details: “The lecture discusses Sputnik and the rocket technology connected with the beginning of the space age. The speaker explains that the Soyuz rocket is still used to take crews to the International Space Station, and its back view is almost indistinguishable from the rocket used half a century ago.”

explanation.text: The transcript mentions Sputnik, identifies the machine as a Soyuz rocket, says it takes crews to the International Space Station, and says the back view is indistinguishable in almost every regard from the rocket that began the space age half a century ago.

misconception.text: If you miss a phrase or hear an unfamiliar word, you should pause mentally and try to work it out before listening further.

correction.text: If part of the lecture is missed or unclear, remain calm and continue listening. If a word is unfamiliar, continue listening because its meaning may not be important or may be explained by what follows.

misconception.text: A strong response only needs accurate content; fluency and pronunciation are secondary extras.

correction.text: The focus of the item type is on content, fluency and pronunciation.

question.text: After listening to a short academic lecture, write five notes only: the topic, two main supporting ideas, one relationship between ideas, and a possible conclusion. Then turn those notes into a 40-second spoken retell.

answer.text: A strong answer starts with a topic sentence, includes the main supporting ideas in a logical order, uses cohesive devices, and is spoken clearly and fluently.

question.text: Create your own abbreviations for these ideas: government, increasing, decreasing, with, without, therefore, about, and number. Then use at least four of them in one set of lecture notes.

answer.text: One possible answer is: gov’t = government; ↑ = increasing; ↓ = decreasing; w/ = with; w/o = without; therefore = therefore; re: = regarding or about; no. = number. A useful note might be: “gov’t policy leads to increasing access without increasing cost; therefore, more participation.”

question.text: Listen to or read a practice passage once. If you miss one detail, continue without stopping. Afterward, retell the topic, main points and any conclusion you can remember.

answer.text: A strong answer does not dwell on the missed detail. It keeps the response organized around the topic, main ideas and conclusion, using remembered information and notes.

question.text: Using the Sputnik transcript topic, prepare a brief retell that mentions Sputnik, the Soyuz rocket, the International Space Station, and the idea that the rocket design has continued from earlier space-age technology.

answer.text: A possible answer: “The lecture is about Sputnik and the rocket technology linked to the beginning of the space age. The speaker explains that the Soyuz rocket takes crews to the International Space Station and that its back view is almost the same as the rocket that began the space age. The main point is that the Russians found a rocket that worked and continued using it.”

review_checklist.text: I can state the topic of a lecture in a clear topic sentence before adding details.
I can identify main supporting ideas and explain how they relate to the main topic.
I can use brief notes, symbols and abbreviations without writing full sentences.
I can keep listening calmly when I miss a word or hear an unfamiliar expression.
I can organize a retell with a topic sentence, supporting ideas, cohesive links and a possible conclusion.
I can practise under the 3-second image preview, 10-second preparation and 40-second response pattern described in this lesson.
I can review my performance for content, oral fluency and pronunciation after a timed retell.
